doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant Interview, 1962-05-17
doc.interviewee: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal and B. Bozant

title: Bunk Johnson's early career and travels
summary: Bunk was playing at 15 or 16, later toured widely and was a professional in New York; Armstrong is said to have played with him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, because after I got 17 years old I left him.
Then I came out of school.
Bunk was out there before you were 17? Oh, yeah. He must have gone mighty early. He must have been a young man himself.
No, no, he was. About 15 or 16 he was playing music. Yeah, sure, yeah.
Well, that's funny. He really got around. He was a lot of places.
Oh, yes. He went to St. Louis with his band. He went to Chicago with his band. He went all of them. He went here with his band. He used to go all around with his band. He didn't use it.
New York? I know you made a big hit in New York in 1945.
Oh, he was professional when he got to New York. He was professional. He was a big-timer. He really was a professional. He used to play. I think Satchimo used to play with him, too.
The other musicians say that. Yeah. That he learned from Bunk.
